title: SLO Contracts & Service Pairing Roadmap - Q2/Q3 2026
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working roadmap for pairing platform engineers with product/feature teams to negotiate SLO contracts, validate observability and runbooks, and run a staged rollout with clear rollback triggers. Focus is on model-serving and API surface (text generation/chat/embeddings) for teams that don't yet have production SLOs defined.

Background and motivation:
- Many feature teams currently rely on ad-hoc latency/availability expectations. That causes frequent confusion during incidents and uneven prioritization of reliability work.
- Platform needs a repeatable, lightweight contract process: (1) define measurable SLOs, (2) validate telemetry and alerts, (3) run an ops onramp pairing sprint, and (4) stage rollout with rollback matrix.
- Goal: reduce mean time to safe rollout by 40% and reduce post-launch P1s by 50% for services paired in this program.

Guiding principles:
- Keep contracts terse: SLI metric, SLO target, measurement window, and ownership. No more than one page per service.
- Prefer SLOs that map to customer-facing impact (error rate, p99 latency for synchronous endpoints, embedding indexing freshness for async flows).
- Automate verification: every pairing must have automated SLI checks in CI or an observability job before rollouts.
- Fail fast: include explicit rollback criteria and automated throttles where possible.

Scope (what this roadmap covers):
- Service types: hosted inference endpoints, dedicated pool frontends, model-router.
- Excludes: internal infra-only components (control plane DBs) — those follow infra SRE backlog.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Platform Engineering (liaison): Olivia Chen (program lead) — coordinates pairings, runbooks, and automation templates.
- Service Owner: product/feature team lead (named per pairing).
- Observability SME: Marcus Green — ensures SLI instrumentation & dashboards.
- SRE Partner: Ravi Menon — on-call integration, runbook sanity checks, incident play validation.
- Legal/Compliance consult: Élodie Laurent (for private deployments with special data controls).

SLO contract template (to be completed during pairing):
- Service name: <string>
- SLI(s): primary SLI (e.g., request_success_rate_by_model), secondary SLI (e.g., p99_decode_latency_ms)
- Target: e.g., 99.9% success over 7d rolling; p99 latency < 700ms over 30d rolling
- Measurement window: 7d/30d/90d as applicable
- Error budget policy: burn thresholds, escalation steps, and auto-throttle behavior
- Observability checks: dashboard link, alert IDs, synthetic test job id
- Rollout acceptance criteria: a set of pass/fail checks for canary phase

Service pairing matrix (example rows):
- pairing-1: model-router -> SLO: global-availability 99.95% (30d); owners: search-product; planned sprint: 2026-04-04 pair sprint with platform; obs link: /d/model-router-slo
- pairing-2: chat-api-v2 -> SLO: success_rate 99.8% (7d), p99 latency < 600ms (30d); owners: chat-team; sprint: 2026-04-18
- pairing-3: embeddings-indexer -> SLO: ingest-freshness < 5m 95% (1d); owners: data-team; sprint: 2026-05-02

Roadmap phases and timeline (high level):
- Phase 0 (preparation, 2 weeks): templates, automation hooks, default alert playbook ready. Owner: platform. (Target complete: 2026-03-01)
- Phase 1 (pilot pairings, 4 weeks): 3 small services (see pairing matrix) to validate process. Include synthetic tests and chaos-lite. (2026-04-04 to 2026-05-01)
- Phase 2 (scale rollout, 8 weeks): onboard 8–10 services in waves of 2/week. Improve templates based on pilot feedback. (2026-05-09 to 2026-07-01)
- Phase 3 (handback & automation, 4 weeks): hand contracts back to service teams, ensure automation of SLI checks and alerting. (2026-07-05 to 2026-07-30)

Acceptance checklist (must pass before broad rollout):
- SLI emitted and visible in dashboards for at least 72 hours.
- Synthetic canary job running and green for 48 hours.
- Incident runbook exists, includes: owner, escalation path, rollback steps, and cost/throughput impact assessment.
- Error budget burn alerts configured with exact throttling/escalation actions.
- Postmortem template agreed for any P1s during canary.

Testing & validation plan:
- Synthetic traffic harness: run at 10x baseline QPS for a 1h soak during canary to exercise backpressure and autoscaling.
- Chaos-lite experiments: simulate a region loss and validate fallback routing for 30m window.
- Regression suite: smoke tests for functionality (generation quality checks are manual but must be flagged to product).
- Observability QA: ensure tag propagation (model_id, route, customer_tier) and correct cardinality in metrics.

Rollback matrix (mapping failures -> action):
- Symptom: p99 latency spikes > 2x baseline during canary for > 15m -> Action: pause rollout, scale-up disabled, route traffic back to baseline version, create P0 bridge if persists
- Symptom: success_rate drops below SLO target by >3x error budget in 1h -> Action: automatic traffic diversion to fallback model, paging to SRE & service owner
- Symptom: downstream infra saturation (GPU OOMs or queue growth) -> Action: immediate rollback and set conservative concurrency limits; open postmortem

Communications & cadence:
- Weekly pairing sync: 30m on Thursdays to surface blockers. Invite list: platform, SRE partner, service owner, observability.
- Daily bridge during canary day 0–2.
- Slack channel naming convention: #slo-onramp-<service-shortname>
- Post-rollout readout: 30m demo and lessons learned doc within 5 business days.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle multi-tenant customers with variable SLAs? (Proposed: per-tenant SLOs only for enterprise tenants; default for shared tenants.)
- Can we automate rollback triggers into the traffic router for Dedicated pools? (Depends on router API work; tracked in ENG-5019.)
- Observability cost: high-cardinality tags may increase metric bill. Need platform quota guidance.

Next concrete steps (owner in parens):
1) Finalize 1-page SLO contract template and check-in with product leads (Olivia). Target: 2026-02-22.
2) Create synthetic harness job and a starter Grafana dashboard template (Marcus). Target: 2026-03-05.
3) Schedule pilot pairings and book protective canary windows (service owners + platform). Target: 2026-03-12.
4) Draft automatic throttle + rollback policy for router (Ravi + infra). Target: 2026-03-19.

Appendix: references and quick links
- Confluence: SLO Contract Template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/SLO+Contract+Template
- Jira: ENG-4921 (synthetic harness), ENG-5019 (router rollback API)
- Runbooks repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep pilot narrow: pick one low-risk internal service to refine alert wording.
- Aim to make the contract digestible for non-SRE engineers; use examples in the template.
- After Phase 1, collect 5 concrete wording edits to the contract and dashboard templates.

If you are reading this and want to join pairing: ping @olivia.chen on Slack with service name, rough traffic profile, and preferred canary week.
